> i continue to question why anyone is a huge fan of chase.

As with almost everything on this sub, people have wildly different priorities and travel habits. If you churn primarily to fly internationally, then I can see why Chase doesn't seem like a big deal to you. But if you rely heavily on Hyatt or Southwest, then they can be immensely valuable.

So do what's best for you. If Chase doesn't bring much value for you, then I totally understand why you don't even care about being at 3/24 soon; sounds like your decision to give minimal spend to Chase is a good one for you. But it's a little bit close-minded and/or disingenuous to question why *anyone* is a huge fan of Chase. It clearly has a lot of value for certain situations.

Looking for DPs ... has anyone had cash back track for purchases made with AMEX cards after 4/1 on apps that run on the Empyr network?

After having several apps basically go dead for over a week, I spent some time last night skimming through the user agreements for the various apps to try to find any type of pattern. Here's what I found:

- Dosh, which uses CFSI as its third-party data company, and Uber, which appears to run using direct Visa data, have worked just fine. Obviously, Uber applies only to Visa transactions, so it doesn't specifically tell us anything about AMEX.

- Yelp (Empyr-based) has been slow to track and/or delayed for all payment processors, but has not tracked AMEX at all.

- PEI and Spent, both Empyr-based, have tracked for Visa and MC, but not AMEX. In fact, with Spent, you can see a list of all transactions that have been passed through to the app by clicking "Review Transactions" in the menu, even if those transactions don't earn anything through Spent. For me, all recent Visa and MC transactions appear, but none for AMEX since 3/31.

Has anyone else had a similar experience lately?

Yeah, I had no problem with AMEX on Yelp prior to 4/1, but have had nothing since. Meanwhile, a couple of Visa purchases from 4/2 came through on 4/7. However, those were organic, not VGC, so it's hard to say for sure whether it's an issue with any particular payment processor, a more general Empyr issue, or if there's been some kind of crackdown specifically on GCs.
Same ... even a pending organic AMEX transaction from 3/31 disappeared on Monday for me.

Did it remove the "claim" from wherever you made the purchase? If not, did they verify that you can use it again?

For example, if you made a purchase at Sam's Club that didn't track, I assume that it still shows up with the "You get 2% Cash Back here" banner. Did that change after Yelp acknowledged the purchase, or is it still there? If it's still there, I'd be concerned that the next purchase won't track either. Did you raise that issue with them?
Which app are you referring to?
Just to clarify ... were the charges made on AMEX cards?

Yes, they each use both Plaid and Empyr, according to their T&Cs. 

I may not be correct on this, but my understanding is that Plaid is the API that connects the banking institutions to the apps. Basically, it's what allows you to enter a single banking login and have all cards from that bank show up instead of having to enter each card manually, as you do for Yelp, which also uses Empyr but not Plaid. I think Empyr is the service that is used to actually track purchases, match them to existing offers, and confirm the cash back.
Awesome, thanks. So it looks like there are a bunch of DPs that match mine, but it's not consistent. I'm stumped.

Update to [yesterday's discussion](https://www.reddit.com/r/churning/comments/ba38hk/manufactured_spending_weekly_thread_week_of_april/ekjt0d4/):
After contacting Pei support about one of many missing transactions, I was told that Plaid is having issues with transaction connections for AMEX and they're trying to fix the issue. So be aware that apps using Plaid to connect to banks could experience continued delays until the problem is resolved.

Gonna tag /u/ld0891 here, since he correctly pointed out yesterday that it could be a Plaid issue and not necessarily an Empyr problem.

TL/DR: Different strokes for different folks

I'll admit that I'm very weird and have a strange little phobia ... I get borderline panic attacks if stuck in a middle seat or window for long periods, as I eventually feel "trapped" if my access the aisle is obstructed for too long. So I will resort to paying people to switch seats in order to get an aisle seat; otherwise, I'd rather not fly at all.

Now with this little nugget in mind, you'd probably think I hate Southwest's seating policy, but the opposite is actually true. While I realize that what follows is probably abnormal based on conversations with others, I've been moved from my "assigned" seats way too frequently on each of the legacy airlines due to changes in aircraft ... and almost always to a middle seat. It's happened often enough that I'm very wary of it every time I fly Delta, United, or AA in particular. When flights are full and you don't have status, it's a real pain.

Southwest, on the other hand, at least gives me a little bit of control. As long as I check in on time, I've always gotten B30 or better. In that position, I've never had a problem getting an aisle seat, as lots of people prefer to take window seats, sit towards the front of the plane regardless of window/middle/aisle, or sit with family or friends.

Southwest's mostly fee-free structure also plays a small role in regards to seating ... 

Due to the legacy airlines' penchant for cancellation fees and my tendency to take lots of short weekend trips for specific events, I'm hesitant to book with a legacy airline too far in advance, as my schedule could change relatively last-minute and preclude me from going. However, in order to get a preferred seat and avoid close-in award booking fees, you have to book at least a few weeks in advance. This creates a conundrum for me: do I book in advance to secure a preferred seat but risk having to cancel at a substantial cost later on, or do I wait, accept close-in booking fees, and risk not having a preferred assigned seat?

With Southwest's cancellation policy, though, it's easy to book speculatively. Well before 24 hours from takeoff, I'll definitely know whether I'm going, so I can check in and basically assure myself an aisle seat. Or, if I can't go, I can cancel basically until the plane doors close and get my points and taxes/fees refunded. Honestly, this still seems like a steal, even though I fly SW about 20-25 times per year.

I think this may have changed more recently, but as of 18-24 months ago, Precheck would get randomly "awarded" for individual flights to passengers who never applied for the program. So some people in the Precheck line honestly didn't know what to do.

My mom -- who is retired and was in the midst of her application for Pre-Check at the time -- arrived at the airport once and realized that she hadn't taken a taser out of her purse that my paranoid dad had put in there for protection when she would go Christmas shopping in the evenings. She did what she thought was the right thing: she walked directly to a TSA agent, explained the situation, and asked what to do with the taser (hand it over to them? throw it away?). 

The TSA agents basically shut down the checkpoint for a few minutes, called additional security (which included a full-body pat-down, including excessive examination of her privates), and interrogated her for over 20 minutes before finally allowing her to board her flight just before the doors closed.

What I'm saying is ... try really hard to avoid bringing a weapon to the airport, even if you're a retired 65-year-old frequent traveler who was going to visit your son and daughter-in-law to help out with their new baby.
TPA is in a nice area. It's right along the bay, adjacent to an upscale mall, secondary business district, and expensive bayfront homes. It also happens to be the best airport in the country, IMO.
On the bright side, the Memphis Delta lounge has more square feet per passenger than any SkyClub I've visited, plus self-serve booze and a staff that actually encouraged me to take a go-cup.

Exactly. She's an honest Southern woman, though, so she did what she thought was right. She was sure they'd calmly say, "Thanks for bringing this to our attention, ma'am. We understand the mistake. We'll discard this for you" and let her be on her way. Noooooope.

I went to Florida, my dad went to LSU. Took him to the 2017 College World Series finals between the two schools. Incredible experience.

Even though the topic asks for trips specifically, I'd like to point out that points can be used for *experiences* for others that you may not be able to fit into the budget with cash. There are obviously the extraordinary examples like the Marriott/SPG experiences that people bid on, but I've been more than happy to cash out MRs through Schwab and even URs through Chase to provide experiences for my parents, despite the "sub-optimal" cpp. 

Last fall, I got all of my aunts and uncles together in my mom's hometown for an upscale dinner to celebrate her retirement and covered the dinner with a big Schwab cash-out. A little further back, I also surprised my dad with floor seats to see the Eagles and the Stones, both of which he saw live back in college in the early 70s and had waxed poetic for years; I used points to offset the cost.

Even though these have been among my lowest cpp redemptions, they've been the most personally valuable for me.

Check the app. You should have a red banner when you select that flight that allows you to change to another routing for free.

I've been told that Southwest's method for changing flights is to book the one nearest to your selected departure time, regardless of number of stops, total length of trip, and arrival time. This seems to be a silly way of doing it, but that's their method. When it does this, you should have 5 days to rebook to a better routing; however, it's best to do it ASAP, just in case the more popular alternate routings fill up (FYI, the auto-changes are usually made on Thursday and Sunday nights, usually around or right at midnight ET, although this isn't always the case).
